newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B index ends down after breaking support.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B index ends down after breaking support.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B shares closed lower on Thursday after selling by some foreign institutions caused the index to fall through the key level at 83 point support level, brokers said.
Amid weak market sentiment, investors bought shares in newly listed Hainan Airlines Co Ltd, which drained away liquidity from the overall market, they said.
The B index fell 1.328 points or 1.59 percent to 82.129 points on volume of 29.799 million shares worth $16.399 million.
"Foreign securities firms were seen unwinding positions to take profit," said one local broker.
The B index had ended the morning session lower as buying of Hainan Airlines caused the broader index to edge down due to lack of investor interest to support the market, brokers said.
But selling gained speed in the afternoon with the growing realization that further gains due to optimism over the return of Hong Kong to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30 were unlikely, they said.
"The return of Hong Kong has been regarded as the major positive news supporting the market, but with the day fast approaching the event has already been digested," the local broker said.
Of 45 B shares, 42 traded with 30 down, seven flat and five up.
Hainan Airlines was both the most actively traded B share counter and the top gainer, ending at $0.536 up $0.066 or 14.04 percent from the issue price of $0.470 yuan.
Huaxin Cement Co. was the sharpest loser on the B share market due to institutional selling. The share fell $0.016 or 7.27 percent to $0.204.
Shanghai's domestic currency A shares fell on similar weak sentiment coupled with two new A share listings, which took attention away from the broader market, brokers said.
The A index fell 13.521 points or one percent to 1,343.199 points on volume of 370.721 million shares worth 5.1 billion yuan.
Sichuan Electrical Apparatus Co. was the biggest A share loser, plunging 0.65 yuan or 6.74 percent to 9.00 yuan.
But the SSE30 blue chip index bucked the trend to edge up 0.983 points or 0.02 percent to 4,137.604 points, boosted by selective buying.
Brokers said they expected Shanghai A and B shares to fall further on Friday.
"With uncertainties for the market after the Hong Kong handover, most investors have little interest in building new positions," one broker said.
"As the market has started a new downward trend, the (B share) index may test support between 78 and 80 points in the short term," added another broker.
